canonical_data: tasks, runs, wakeup requests, approvals, budget policies, cost events, routines, goals, and pipelines in a Postgres database the server embeds by default, plus per-run execution workspaces on the host
strengths: The orchestration state is real and persisted: the schema holds tasks, heartbeat runs, a queued wakeup table with coalescing, approvals, routines with cron, webhook and API triggers, and pipelines, and the server reads them back to decide what each agent does next

Spend is a first-class control rather than a dashboard: scoped budget policies carry warning thresholds and a hard stop, backed by recorded cost events, and the README says plainly that in-flight work can delay a stop

The adapter set is broad and symmetric, with separate packages for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, Grok, Kimi, Hermes and two gateway protocols, plus a plugin loader for outside adapters
weaknesses: The repository is under eight months old and carries 2,801 open issues and 3,389 open pull requests, with calendar-versioned releases every few days
The README labels agent chat, chat and email connectors, and pipelines experimental, and the roadmap calls its own list directional rather than promised
It does not run an agent loop of its own: its adapters start installed vendor CLIs, so reliability and cost accounting depend on what those tools report
Hosted use is a waitlist; the LICENSE names Paperclip AI while the README footer names Paperclip Labs, Inc
why_it_matters: The clearest example of a control plane that treats competing vendors' coding agents as employees, with a ledger, a budget, and an approval path in place of a terminal multiplexer.
